name: Foreign Investor / Foreign Management Personnel (Investment Law 2016-71)

requirements.blocker_text: As foreign management personnel of a Tunisian enterprise, must fall within the statutory quota: up to 30% of total management staff (or a minimum of 4 foreign managers, whichever is more favorable) during the enterprise's first 3 years, reducing to 10% thereafter. Recruitment beyond this quota requires separate Ministry of Employment authorization under the Labour Code.

evidence_required.document: Enterprise registration and management-staff headcount records

outcome.duration_length: not specified precisely in the sources located in this build

sources.title: UNCTAD Investment Policy Hub -- Tunisia Investment Law: Article 3 defines investment broadly with no minimum capital threshold specified; Article 6 caps foreign management-staff recruitment at 30% of total management staff (or 4 persons minimum, whichever is more favorable) for the first 3 years of operation, reducing to 10% thereafter, with recruitment beyond the quota requiring separate Ministry of Employment authorization; Article 7 grants foreign investors national treatment (no less favorable than Tunisian investors) for rights and obligations under the law

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Tunisia). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 sourcing only (UNCTAD's Investment Policy Hub); Tunisia's own government hosting of the Investment Law (2016-71) was not successfully located and fetched in this build. GENUINE FINDING, NOT A GAP: the law explicitly does NOT set a minimum capital investment threshold -- unlike most business/investor routes built elsewhere in this dataset (contrast Ghana's tiered $200k/$500k/$1M structure, or Kenya's $100k Class G threshold), Tunisia's law instead gates foreign PERSONNEL through a management-staff quota rather than gating the INVESTMENT itself through a capital floor. This means the modeled hard requirement here is about staffing composition, not investment size -- a structurally different mechanism worth flagging precisely rather than assuming a capital threshold exists and is simply unsourced. The law itself does not appear to confer residence or work-permit entitlements directly (per the source's own reading); actual work authorization for foreign management staff presumably still runs through the general carte de séjour process (see tn_work_permit.json).
